decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. In Studies 2 and 3, the authors empirically administer standard comparative-plus-estimation anchoring trials alongside incidental anchoring items, explicitly stating in Study 2 Method (p. 6) that these items enabled a replication of the classic anchoring procedure designed by Tversky and Kahneman (1974) and reporting robust anchoring effects in the Results of Studies 2 and 3 (pp. 6, 8) and the Meta-Analysis (pp. 9-10). The reference list (p. 15) and Crossref metadata identify the original as Tversky, A., & Kahneman, D. (1974), 'Judgment under uncertainty: Heuristics and biases,' Science, 185, 1124-1131, DOI 10.1126/science.185.4157.1124. This classic standard anchoring paper is completely distinct from shipped rows 1475 (Critcher & Gilovich, 2007/2008, DOI 10.1002/bdm.586) and 1494 (Dogerlioglu-Demir & Koçaş, 2014/2015, DOI 10.1007/s11002-014-9295-0) as well as sibling target 2 (Koçaş & Dogerlioglu-Demir, 2020, DOI 10.1016/j.jbusres.2019.01.027), all of which test incidental environmental anchoring.

decisions.reason: Luna's triage mistakenly matched Koçaş & Dogerlioglu-Demir (2020; Journal of Business Research, 109, 536–544, DOI 10.1016/j.jbusres.2019.01.027) to shipped row 1494, which is actually the earlier distinct paper Dogerlioglu-Demir & Koçaş (2014/2015; Marketing Letters, 26, 607–618, DOI 10.1007/s11002-014-9295-0, sibling target 1; shipped row 1475 is Critcher & Gilovich, 2007/2008, sibling target 0). However, whether the current study (Shanks et al., 2020) empirically retests a specific published finding from Koçaş & Dogerlioglu-Demir (2020) remains genuinely ambiguous. Although the General Discussion explicitly states that their procedure is a close replication of the equivalent studies by Critcher & Gilovich (2008), Dogerlioglu-Demir & Koçaş (2015), and Koçaş & Dogerlioglu-Demir (2020), Studies 1–3 test direct positive high versus low restaurant anchors (Studio 97 vs. Studio 17), the Meta-Analysis and Note 2 pool only Critcher & Gilovich (2008) and Dogerlioglu-Demir & Koçaş (2015), and Note 1 states that Koçaş & Dogerlioglu-Demir (2020) explored how ambiguous anchor values (e.g., negative values) are interpreted. Because the 2020 primary full text is inaccessible in follow-up 0097 and its repository abstract describes shifting-decimal, negative, and inverse number associations without confirming whether a direct positive 17/97 WTP contrast was also tested, correspondence cannot be determined.
